![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14188718/assets/63fe9cf3a61a5cef09f9c19e16a18318338faa6837eeb77b83f49b636157bb95.png)

A sphere is decreasing in volume at a rate of $54\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}\text{/s}.$ Calculate the rate at which the radius of the sphere is decreasing at the moment when the radius is $3\,\text{cm}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $r$ be the radius of the balloon and $V$ its volume. Both $r$ and $V$ change with time. In particular, we are given

$$
\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=-54\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{s},
$$

and we want to find $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}$ when $r=3\,\text{cm}.$

To start, let's write down the volume formula for the sphere and then differentiate it using implicit differentiation. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(V) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}r}(\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot 4\pi {r}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=-54\pi $ and $r=3,$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}-54\pi  & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot 4\pi (3)^{2} \\ -54\pi  & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot 36\pi  \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =-1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of the sphere is decreasing at a rate of $1.5\text{ cm/s}$ when the radius is $3\,\text{cm}.$
